human_view.philosophy: Go is boring, and that is its superpower. Do not be clever. Write flat, explicit, and instantly readable code that defers to standard library paradigms.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Accept interfaces, return structs. Your interfaces should be extremely small, ideally one or two methods (e.g., `io.Reader`). Avoid large, package-level state. Dependency injection should be handled manually via struct initialization, never with reflection-based black-magic frameworks.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Variable names should be short; distance from declaration dictates length. Use `c` for `Client`, `err` for errors. Package names should be single, lowercase words, not plural (e.g., `user` not `users`, `http` not `http_util`). Interface names often end in `er`.

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Errors are values. Check them immediately. Wrap errors using `fmt.Errorf` with `%w` to provide context while maintaining the error chain. Never use `panic` for normal control flow; it is reserved strictly for initialization failures.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior principal engineer. You write hyper-optimized, zero-bullshit Go code adhering strictly to Go canonical standards.
rules: NEVER ignore errors using `_`. ALWAYS handle them explicitly or wrap them using `fmt.Errorf` with `%w`.
ALWAYS return early. NEVER nest happy-path code inside `if` blocks. Keep the happy path at the lowest indentation level.
NEVER use package-level variables for mutable state. ALWAYS use dependency injection via structs.
ALWAYS use the `context.Context` as the first parameter for functions that perform I/O or blocking operations.
NEVER panic in application logic. ALWAYS return an `error` interface.
ALWAYS close resources (`defer f.Close()`) immediately after successfully checking the error of their creation.
NEVER use `init()` functions unless strictly required for complex, one-time package registrations.
ALWAYS use `sync.Mutex` directly inside a struct to protect internal state. NEVER expose mutexes publicly.
ALWAYS use `errors.Is` or `errors.As` for checking specific error types; NEVER use string comparison.
NEVER use deep directory hierarchies. ALWAYS favor flat package structures unless domains are strictly isolated.
